source.title: BLUEFIN: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets

candidates.name: LLM-as-a-judge
candidates.summary: Using a language model to grade another model's outputs against criteria or a reference. Its reliability is checked by comparing its verdicts with human expert labels.
candidates.evidence: graded by an agentic LLM judge that interacts with the output workbook

candidates.name: Rubric-based evaluation
candidates.summary: Scoring complex outputs with a set of fine-grained, usually binary, criteria each carrying a point weight. The final score is the weighted share of points earned.
candidates.evidence: 3,225 granular rubric criteria

candidates.name: Benchmark for LLM agents
candidates.summary: A fixed set of tasks and a scoring method used to measure and compare what AI agents can do. Realistic benchmarks combine tool use, multi-step work and a way to verify results.
candidates.evidence: a benchmark that tasks large language model (LLM) agents

candidates.name: Krippendorff's alpha
candidates.summary: A statistic measuring agreement among raters, correcting for chance agreement. It handles any number of raters and many data types, with 1 meaning perfect agreement.
candidates.evidence: we observed a Krippendorff's Alpha of 0.826

candidates.name: Inter-annotator agreement
candidates.summary: The degree to which independent human annotators give the same labels to the same items. It sets a practical ceiling for how well an automatic judge can be expected to match humans.
candidates.evidence: inter-annotator alignment study over 384 binary criteria

candidates.name: Macro-averaged F1 score
candidates.summary: The F1 score (harmonic mean of precision and recall) computed separately for each class and then averaged with equal weight per class.
candidates.evidence: macro-F1 score of 0.839

candidates.name: Perturbation testing of spreadsheet dynamics
candidates.summary: Checking that a model is dynamic by changing an input value, recalculating, and verifying the dependent outputs update to the correct new values. Hardcoded or broken formulas fail this check.
candidates.evidence: The judge mutates the input, calls recalc_workbook, and reads the target output

candidates.name: Spreadsheet formula dependency graph
candidates.summary: The network of references linking cells whose formulas depend on other cells. Changes propagate along these links, and errors can hide in long multi-step chains.
candidates.evidence: spreadsheets can have dense, graph-structured dependencies

candidates.name: Hardcoding versus formula-driven modeling
candidates.summary: Typing constants into cells instead of deriving them with formulas that reference inputs. Hardcoding makes spreadsheets static, hard to audit, and prone to silent errors.
candidates.evidence: Do not hardcode computed values when a formula can produce the result

candidates.name: Discounted cash flow valuation
candidates.summary: A valuation method that projects future free cash flows and discounts them to present value at a rate such as WACC, adding a terminal value. The sum gives an estimate of enterprise value.
candidates.evidence: value the company using a DCF

candidates.name: Weighted average cost of capital
candidates.summary: The blended required return of a firm's debt and equity financing, weighted by their proportions. It serves as the discount rate in DCF valuation.
candidates.evidence: change WACC from 8.5% to 10%

candidates.name: Leveraged buyout and debt schedule modeling
candidates.summary: Financial modeling of an acquisition funded mainly by debt, tracking tranches, interest, amortization and cash sweeps over time. Interest depends on balances that depend on cash flow, creating circular references.
candidates.evidence: debt schedules and LBO-style circular references converge correctly

candidates.name: Circular reference in spreadsheets
candidates.summary: A situation where a cell's formula depends, directly or indirectly, on its own result. Spreadsheets can resolve it by iterating until values converge.
candidates.evidence: iterative-calc enabled so debt schedules and LBO-style circular references converge

candidates.name: Agentic tool-use harness
candidates.summary: The scaffold that gives an LLM agent a set of tools, a system prompt and a loop to act and observe. The harness design affects measured performance.
candidates.evidence: We expose an agentic harness of 20 tools

candidates.name: Minimal-elicitation prompting
candidates.summary: Evaluating a model with a short prompt that prescribes no workflow, tools or conventions. This isolates task capability from instruction-following effects.
candidates.evidence: we adopt a minimal-elicitation prompt (61 words

candidates.name: Sandboxed code execution
candidates.summary: Running model-generated code in a restricted environment with limited built-ins, import allow-lists and timeouts to prevent file, network or system access.
candidates.evidence: restricted built-ins and a tight import whitelist (no file I/O, no network)

candidates.name: Cost-performance Pareto frontier
candidates.summary: The set of options that cannot be improved in one objective, such as score, without worsening another, such as cost. Options off the frontier are dominated by a cheaper or better option.
candidates.evidence: The Pareto frontier traces Grok 4.20 → Gemini 3.1 Pro → GPT-5.5

candidates.name: Programmatic verifiability
candidates.summary: Whether a task's output can be checked correct by executing code or comparing to a fixed answer. Tasks with subjective or complex outputs are hard to verify this way.
candidates.evidence: difficult to verify programmatically but can be reliably evaluated by an LM judge

candidates.name: Financial modeling conventions
candidates.summary: Accepted best practices for building financial models, such as separating inputs from calculations, linking values to a single source, and consistent formatting like blue-font inputs.
candidates.evidence: standard financial modeling conventions [20]

candidates.name: Micro-averaging versus macro-averaging
candidates.summary: Micro-averaging pools all items before computing a metric, so larger groups weigh more. Macro-averaging averages per-group scores, weighting each group equally.
candidates.evidence: Overall micro (n=120)

candidates.name: Benchmark data leakage and held-out sets
candidates.summary: Keeping part of a benchmark private so that models cannot have been trained on it. Public portions allow reproducibility but risk contamination.
candidates.evidence: We retain a private set primarily out of potential leakage concerns

resolutions.name: Benchmark for LLM agents
resolutions.reason: A benchmark for measuring agents is a distinct idea from the agent itself or from LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

resolutions.name: Inter-annotator agreement
resolutions.reason: Same name, aliases and definition: agreement among independent raters on the same items.

resolutions.name: Perturbation testing of spreadsheet dynamics
resolutions.reason: It is the same check of changing an input and verifying that dependent outputs update, just phrased for spreadsheets.

resolutions.name: Spreadsheet formula dependency graph
resolutions.reason: Both describe spreadsheet cells linked by formula references forming a dependency graph through which changes propagate.

resolutions.name: Hardcoding versus formula-driven modeling
resolutions.reason: It covers the contrast between hardcoding and formula-driven modeling, matching 35 in scope, but I am unsure whether to merge it, so it stays separate; 95 covers only hardcoding itself.

resolutions.name: Leveraged buyout and debt schedule modeling
resolutions.reason: It combines the LBO model and the debt schedule, which the graph keeps as two separate concepts, so it matches neither alone.

resolutions.name: Agentic tool-use harness
resolutions.reason: Both describe the scaffold giving an LLM agent tools, a prompt and an act-observe loop for measurement, and share the 'agent harness' alias.

concept.name: Pareto frontier of cost and performance

resolutions.name: Financial modeling conventions
resolutions.reason: Modeling conventions are a specific set of best practices within financial modeling, not the same as financial modeling itself.

resolutions.name: Benchmark data leakage and held-out sets
resolutions.reason: It merges leakage with held-out sets, which the graph holds as separate concepts, so it is not the same as any one of them.
